answer: Each identity must hold one registered appellation orchard, checked against the registry: one orchard backs exactly one identity, duplicates rejected. Appellations are capped by region, so a farm cannot mint more. Per fake the attacker buys one orchard for 5,000 units and waits 180 days for inspection, its karst soil proving the terroir. The cheapest cheat is renting an orchard, but its owner then surrenders the appellation backing their own identity, and a rental still costs 1,200 units a season. One orchard anchors one identity. 100 fakes need 100 orchards: 500,000 units, 18,000 days.
